title: Best Logo Designers on Fiverr (2026): How to Hire One and Get a Logo You'll Keep
description: How to hire a logo designer on Fiverr: what a good package includes, how to write the brief, which files you need, and the red flags to avoid.
intro: A logo is cheap to order and expensive to change later, once it is on your website, packaging and social profiles. Whether you keep it or replace it within a year usually comes down to two things: the brief you write and the files you ask for. This guide covers both.

faq.q: Which logo files do I actually need?
faq.a: At minimum a vector file (SVG, AI, EPS or PDF) that can scale to any size, plus PNG files with a transparent background for everyday use. Ask for full-color, black and white versions, and a square icon version for social profiles.

faq.q: Do I own the logo after the order?
faq.a: Only if the gig says so. Many packages list copyright transfer or commercial use as part of a higher tier or an extra. Confirm in writing before ordering that you receive full rights to the final design.

faq.q: How many concepts should I ask for?
faq.a: Two or three distinct concepts is usually enough. More concepts often means less time spent on each. It is better to pick one strong direction early and use your revisions to refine it.

faq.q: Should I use a logo maker or hire a designer?
faq.a: A logo maker such as Fiverr Logo Maker is quick and inexpensive, and works well for new or small projects. Hiring a designer takes longer and costs more, but you get a design created from scratch around your brief, which matters if you plan to trademark it.

faq.q: Can a logo designer use AI or templates?
faq.a: Some do, which is why originality matters. Ask whether the design is created from scratch, and run a reverse image search on the final logo before you use it. A logo copied from a template or stock site cannot be trademarked and may already be used by someone else.

faq.q: What should I do if I don't like the first concepts?
faq.a: Give specific feedback: what feels wrong (too playful, too busy, wrong color) and point to examples you like. Vague feedback such as 'make it pop' leads to rounds of guessing and uses up your revisions.
